sections.h2: Which sale method makes sense for a Rock Island owner?
sections.html:
Owners here can hire an agent to list the house, market it themselves, or accept an offer from a buyer paying cash who is willing to take the property as it is. Repairs, timing and whether the building is a home or a rental drive the choice.

Rock Island is one of the Quad Cities, alongside Moline and East Moline in Illinois and Davenport and Bettendorf in Iowa, so the buyer pool crosses the river. A tidy house can do well on the open market. One that needs work, carries a tenant or sits on a rental-heavy block may be better matched to a direct sale. Weigh these points:

  • Putting the house on the market reaches the most shoppers, though repairs and open-house hours usually come with it.
  • Selling privately skips the agent's commission and leaves marketing, paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • A direct purchase for cash can close without a lender's appraisal, which keeps the schedule in your hands.
  • If the property is a rental, the city's rental license and inspection rules may come into play first.

Whichever way you go, have the price, closing date and cost split in writing before you commit.

sections.h2: What is the Rock Island housing picture in the Census data?
sections.html:
Home prices in Rock Island run modest. The five-year Census survey ending in 2024 puts the middle value of a house occupied by its owner at $125,900, and roughly 35 percent of occupied units are rented.

A rental should be priced with area rents in mind, because an investor works backward from what tenants pay, and the middle gross rent is $842.

sections.h2: How do the rivers, the Arsenal and the neighborhoods shape a Rock Island sale?
sections.html:
The city sits where the Rock River meets the Mississippi, and Arsenal Island, the original Rock Island, lies in the Mississippi between Rock Island and Davenport. Rock Island Arsenal is the largest government-owned weapons manufacturing arsenal in the United States and employs about 6,000 people, so the base accounts for a large part of the local job market.

The city's older pockets each have their own character:

  • Downtown and the Broadway Historic District, with well-preserved late 1800s and early 1900s buildings.
  • Watch Hill and the southern part of the city, once the separate community of Searstown and annexed in 1915.
  • The blocks around Augustana College, which was founded in 1860.
  • Streets near the Mississippi riverfront, home to Schwiebert Riverfront Park and a casino.

Rock Island is also an old rail town. The Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad was founded here in 1851. Bridges cross to Davenport, including the Government Bridge, the Centennial Bridge and the Interstate 280 bridge, and Quad Cities MetroLINK buses use District Station downtown as a hub.

sections.h2: Which employers and schools matter to Rock Island buyers?
sections.html:
In its 2017 annual financial report the city ranked Rock Island Arsenal first with 6,301 employees, ahead of Trinity Rock Island with 1,848 and Rock Island-Milan School District 41 with 1,292. County government, Jumer's Casino and Hotel, Augustana College and Modern Woodmen of America each employ several hundred more.

District 41, Rock Island-Milan, covers the bulk of the city with 13 public schools, among them Rock Island High School. Some southwest addresses belong to Rockridge. Jordan Catholic Elementary School and Alleman Catholic High School serve private-school families.

An address close to a district line deserves a call to the district before you advertise it. Plenty of shoppers narrow their search by school district before they look at streets.

sections.h2: What is Rock Island's history, and how does it show in older houses?
sections.html:
The oldest part of the city was called Farnhamsburg, after homes built in 1826 by two trading partners. A plat was filed in 1835 under the name Stephenson, and the town took the name Rock Island in March 1841. The Rock Island Arsenal has produced equipment for the U.S. Army since the 1880s and was established in 1862, and it is a National Historic Landmark.

Two hotels, the Harper House and the Rock Island House, opened during the late 1800s. Chippiannock Cemetery dates to 1854, and the public library was established in 1872. A new Rock Island County courthouse was built from 2017 to 2018 at a cost of $28 million. These details matter to a seller mostly because they show how much of the city dates from the 1800s and early 1900s. Older houses can carry original wiring, plaster and stone foundations, and a buyer will want to know what has been updated.

sections.h2: What does Rock Island require for rental properties before a sale?
sections.html:
City ordinance calls for a rental license on every residential rental, and each unit has to pass an inspection against a minimum code standard before it is offered to tenants. Landlords apply through the city's self-service portal, and the Inspection Division sends an email to schedule the inspection after the rental fee is paid.

Inspections are scheduled with the owner or a designated agent, who must be present, and a cancellation fee of $50 applies if the owner does not appear or cancel 24 hours ahead. A Notice of Violation lists items that fail life safety requirements. The first re-inspection is free, and additional compliance inspections cost $50 each. The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time.

A license does not release the owner from fixing violations. Planning to sell a rental? Clear any open violations or tell the buyer about them, and ask the Inspection Division at 1528 Third Avenue where your license stands before you list.

sections.h2: How is a Rock Island deed recorded and which transfers are exempt from tax?
sections.html:
Deeds for Rock Island parcels are recorded with the Rock Island County Recorder. The office's fee schedule, set by county ordinance effective February 1, 2025, lists $83 for a conforming document with no page count, $64 for certain exempt document types, and $104 for a non-conforming document or one with more than five references. Any document with a legal description also needs the 10-digit PIN.

The state transfer tax statute exempts a list of transfers from the tax, and some of them still require the declaration to be filed. Section 31-45 of the Property Tax Code lists these among the exempt items: deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100, tax deeds, deeds of partition, deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier deed, deeds to or from government bodies and charities, and deeds given to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or as a substitute for it. A normal sale to a buyer does not fall in these categories.

Rock Island County offers a no-cost Property Fraud Alert subscription that sends a notice whenever a filing mentions you. Someone leaving a house empty for a while may want to enroll first.

faqs.q: Do I need a city rental license in order to sell a rented Rock Island house?
faqs.a: The license applies to renting a unit, so selling does not need one. Open inspection violations on a rented house can still slow a sale, so ask the Inspection Division where your file stands.

faqs.q: How much do Rock Island houses cost?
faqs.a: The survey figure for the middle owner-occupied home is $125,900. An individual house can land far above or below it, depending on size, condition and block.

faqs.q: Where is a Rock Island deed recorded?
faqs.a: Rock Island County. Its Recorder's Office lists conforming documents at $83 and non-conforming documents at $104 under a fee schedule effective February 1, 2025. Confirm the current figure before closing.

faqs.q: What school district is my Rock Island house in?
faqs.a: Rock Island-Milan School District 41 covers most addresses. A few in the southwest belong to Rockridge, so verify yours with the district.
About 36,225 people lived here in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. Rock Island holds the county seat and counts among the Quad Cities.
